newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Shell, H.Leong top S.Lanka products tender offers.
newsitem.headline: Shell, H.Leong top S.Lanka products tender offers.

text.p: Shell Singapore and Hin Leong Trading have placed the most competitive offers to Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp's (CPC) tenders to buy diesel, jet fuel and gasoline, company sources said Thursday.
Shell Singapore offered premiums of $1.63 per barrel and $1.71 to spot Singapore quotes for the sale of 185,000 barrels of 1.0 percent sulphur gas oil and 40,000 barrels of jet fuel, respectively.
Both cargoes were offered on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Colombo for delivery between January 23-24.

Singapore-based trader Hin Leong offered premiums of $1.86 per barrel and $3.45 to spot Singapore quotes for the sale of 185,000 barrels of 1.0 percent sulphur gas oil and 85,000 barrels of 85 to 88-octane leaded gasoline, respectively.
Both cargoes were offered on a c-and-f basis to Colombo for delivery between January 29-30.

CPC bought its last 1.0-percent sulphur diesel at a premium of $1.57 per barrel to Singapore spot quotes, while the jet fuel was bought at a $1.77 premium to Singapore spot quotes, both on a c-and-f basis to Colombo for delivery between January 15-16.

Traders said the scheduled 45-day shutdown of the Sapugaskanda 60,000 barrels-per-day refinery from mid-January had led to increased diesel and jet fuel purchases as well as the rare import of a gasoline cargo.
